title: Moral evil, and physical good contrasted with moral good
source_text: II. Hujus boni oppositum est malum illud quod poenam & vituperium meretur, quod malum culpae solet appellari, & sub se omnia vitia & peccata comprehendit. Ab hoc vero bono contradistinguitur bonum quod dicitur Physicum, seu naturae, quod scilicet, a nostra voluntate non pendet, & naturam ita perficit, ut non propterea laus, vel praemium quoddam nobis debeatur, nec ab eo simpliciter boni denominemur.
pass_a_gloss: II. The opposite of this good is that evil which deserves punishment and blame, which is wont to be called the evil of fault, and comprehends under itself all vices and sins. But from this good is distinguished the good which is called Physical, or of nature, which namely does not depend on our will, and so perfects nature that not on that account is praise, or some reward owed to us, nor are we from it called good simply.
pass_b_english: Its opposite is the evil that deserves punishment and blame. This is usually called the evil of fault, and it includes all vices and sins.

Set against this good is the good called physical, or the good of nature. It does not depend on our will, and it perfects our nature without earning us any praise or reward; it does not make us good without qualification.

choices.why: The Schools' term for the good that earns praise or reward and makes a man good without qualification; kept as 'moral good', with the narrower Roman sense explained in the text.
